entry.title: Add default santizer config
entry.content:
This add information on the Sanitizer default configuration and cross links it where needed.
@wbamberg @evilpie - would appreciate your review.

The information is specified in two places.

  1. An overview in the API overview page. This provides the gist and links to ...
  2. A separate guide page with a slightly expanded explanation, and a listing of the values.

I chose to do it in two docs , because the "full listing" is too much information for most users. I chose to put the "summary version" in the overview guide rather than in Sanitizer() because it is relevant to everything and worth knowing up front.

In addition, I made lots of minor spot changes that reflected a long-standing lack of understanding (mine) of the purpose of the default config vs the baseline remove config.

Essentially the default config removes more than just XSS-unsafe stuff - so this is more restrictive than what you get if you start with a custom config and call removeUnsafe on it.
The implication of the docs before this chang was that removeUnsafe would get you back to the default config.
The changes might still allow you to infer that in some cases, but I think I've been pretty clear that they are different now.

Related docs work can be tracked in #42755

Fixes #43226

entry.title: Fix DOMPurify usage
entry.content:
Many examples use DOMPurify.sanitize() to create Trusted Type policies without unsetting the RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE flag, in which case this method might return a TrustedHTML object directly. DOMPurify explicitly requires unsetting the RETURN_TRUSTED_TYPE flag during policy creation.

Unlike TrustedTypePolicy.createHTML(), the createHTML method of the policy option argument of TrustedTypePolicyFactory.createPolicy() should return a string instead of a TrustedHTML object.

This PR fixes all such usages, with some minor changes:

  • Unifies all policy names to "my-policy".
  • Adds missing links to DOMPurify references.
  • Replaces the SAFE_FOR_JQUERY flag in an example. The flag is already removed.

entry.title: docs: add animal idiom alternatives to inclusive language guide
entry.content:
Summary

Closes #43242.

Following reviewer consensus in the issue thread, this is a narrowly scoped addition to the "Use inclusive language" section of the Writing Style Guide. It adds guidance to avoid figurative idioms that use animals in violent or harmful contexts, with plain-English alternatives for three common phrases:

  • "kill two birds with one stone" → "solve two problems at once"
  • "beating a dead horse" → "belaboring the point" or "going in circles"
  • "more than one way to skin a cat" → "more than one way to do this"

Explicitly excluded per reviewer feedback in the issue: technical terms like kill (Unix command), monkey-patching, and dogfooding — these are well-established technical vocabulary and replacing them would introduce confusion without benefit.

entry.title: [Technical review] BiDi - Add pages for new, status, and end commands of the session module

Description

entry.title: Clarify AudioBufferSourceNode.buffer behavior for null values
entry.content:
Description

Clarified that when buffer is set to null, the node outputs silence and stops immediately if start() has been called. The null behavior description has been moved to the Value section for better organization.

Motivation

According to the W3C Web Audio API specification, if buffer is null and start() has been called, the node stops immediately.

The current documentation only stated that the node "generates silence," which could lead readers to assume the node continues playing indefinitely (outputting zeros) until stop() is called manually. This update clarifies that the node stops immediately.

entry.title: fix: update outdated Firefox-only warning for <select> keyboard selec…
entry.content:
…tion (closes #43145)

Updates outdated documentation claiming Firefox-only support for non-contiguous keyboard selection. Adjusted wording to reflect broader compatibility while maintaining caution.

Description

Updates the outdated warning in the <select> element documentation that stated non-contiguous keyboard selection only works in Firefox. The wording has been revised to reflect broader browser compatibility while maintaining caution about platform-specific behavior.

Motivation

The current documentation states that non-contiguous keyboard selection only works in Firefox. However, the feature is marked as widely available in compatibility data and appears to function across modern browsers. Updating the warning prevents readers from receiving outdated or misleading browser support information.

Additional details

No functional changes were made. This update only revises documentation wording to align with current compatibility information shown on the page.
